1hsbugb: Mistake one: holding on to the reins. Hold yourself on with your balance instead, not with the horse's mouth. Mistake two: looking down. Always look ahead!
d7j323: Mistake three: drawing your heels up and squeezing your knees together. Let your leg hang long and keep your heel down. And don't forget to breathe!
1de6d8p: Hands: holding on to the reins, flat hands (backs of the hands on top), restless or too-low hands, and reins that are too long or too short. Correct: upright fists, thumbs on top like a roof, a straight line from elbow to hand to the horse's mouth.
1umunu6: Seat: looking down, upper body in front of or behind the vertical, chair seat with legs too far forward, drawn-up heels, gripping knees. Correct: eyes ahead, ear – shoulder – hip – heel line, leg long and relaxed against the horse, heel the lowest point. Many mistakes are linked: if you grip, you get pushed up and hold on to the reins.
19mxwxg: Aids: constant tapping with the leg makes the horse dull, and constant pulling makes the mouth hard. Correct: a short, clear aid – wait for the response – give – praise. Holding your breath and tensing up also transfer to the horse. Breathe out calmly and deliberately.

xvxzh5: If your horse spooks: stay calm, sit upright, look ahead and keep your legs on. Talk calmly to your horse and ride it onto a big curve.
6q3bd3: Training your balance: seat exercises on the lunge (arm circles, hands on hips, without stirrups), lots of rising trot and work in a light seat, vaulting and exercise outside the yard. A balanced seat is safer than any gripping technique.
2dpgok: If the horse spooks: sit deep and upright, eyes ahead, leg long against the horse, don't snatch the reins up.
